In the wild, thy name is whispered with reverence, yet also with yearning, For none but thee could tame our souls, wild things made tame. Such was thy lesson, O pale ancient guard. Thou hast taught us, and our world has changed: Thou hast given insects reason and powers we never prayed for. Our cherished dreams, which thou hast granted and magnified, Yet too late in dismay we knew our desires were endless. What price to curb our ferocity? Thou hast given all — and more. But the desires remained unquenchable, endless dreams, Draining thy strength away. Among them came a dire calamity, Forcing us back to our aggressive urges, Transforming us back to beasts and shells, Our souls devoured by the light from above. Within thy corpse yet sounds the true cry of him Who bore our pain, our losses, our dreams within him, that… Through his pain we found the truth that must be acknowledged, For naught can contain such things save absolute emptiness.
